GOAL: read the five frozen evidence bundles and place the five proposals one to one under selection policy rank-2026-10-v1.
WHAT I READ: all five bundles (l1pdo-rq e10be3a2caf57e91, DEMARGIN-L1-CURV aa31432fc3e0b58b, pmi-geomargin-l1-rq 27b5ac51b79ed630, BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ 2a311217eab4a282, GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ 5dee08eef77d0f88). The behavioural and geometric entries (E1-E3, E12-E13) are PROPOSED text in every bundle; the only OBSERVED, reusable evidence is E4-E11, and it is identical across the five bundles.
OBSERVED (the load-bearing numbers): (a) E6 width-20 beam survival - l1_br recall@10 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500; gold prefix alive at depth 1 is 1.000 for the level-1 beam arms, and the attrition is at depths 2/3 (l1_br_euclid 0.829/0.161) and depth 4 (l1_br 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068). (b) E7 teacher-forced NLL: l1_br T1/T2/T3 = 0.00/0.00/0.00, l1_br_euclid 0.00/3.22/4.36. (c) E8 first-level capacity ceiling on frozen Stage1 vectors: share of canonical pairs sharing a K cluster = 0.3106 (K=16), 0.1547 (K=64), 0.0822 (K=256). (d) E5 successor-entropy stratification: top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the lowest quintile vs 0.0543 in the highest, Spearman -0.973, so the transition mass is heavily skewed toward a few successors. (e) E9 cohort-profile signal: positive shares a successor cohort with its anchor 0.9291 vs 0.8871 for negatives, 0.5898 of pairs beat all ten negatives. (f) E10/E11: 118315 train edges, mean out-degree 5.45; baseline same-first-prefix rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067.
REASONING: all five proposals are the same mechanism class - keep K1=256, lift the level-1 residual and the baseline level-1 codebook into a Poincare ball, score with d_c, and subtract a detached per-codeword behaviour offset before the argmin, leaving levels 2-3, the loss and the STE at baseline. So they must be separated on (i) how the offset is scaled in distance units, (ii) whether the behaviour statistic is popularity-debiased, (iii) whether curvature is strong enough not to be a no-op, (iv) collapse risk under a single run. E6 shows that mild/coarse geodesic-successor level-1 arms scored 0.0546-0.0550, i.e. at/below baseline, and that the best frozen arms (0.0621-0.0636) used neither behaviour nor curvature, so aggressive one-sided level-1 displacement (l1_br 0.0467) is the demonstrated failure mode. Best scale is therefore an offset tied to the measured mean nearest-code geodesic distance, not to the full distance spread. That puts pmi-geomargin (10% of mean min_k D_k, doubly popularity-adjusted, online surplus refresh) first, l1pdo-rq second (live curved-softmax loop and c=1 so curvature is not near-Euclidean, zero-mean symmetric offset), BEABLATE third (correct curved-unit scaling but c=0.25 and lambda=1/72000 make it near-static and near-Euclidean), GEOMARGIN fourth (zero-mean margin is clean but z is frozen from BASELINE Euclidean assignments and c=1 with a 10% cap is likely a no-op), DEMARGIN last (offset scale = mean half-spread, clamped to 0..3w, the largest and one-sided displacement, plus admitted atanh boundary risk).
STILL OPEN: none of these touches depth 2/3, where E6/E7 locate the loss for the strongest frozen arms (l1_br_euclid 0.829/0.161), and E8 caps the K=256 first-level share at 0.0822; that is the objection recorded with the ranking. Next record carries

COMPLETE ANSWER (final record, stands on its own).
Ranking of the five proposals, best first, under rank-2026-10-v1, grounded in the frozen OBSERVED entries E5/E6/E7/E8/E9 of the bundles (E1-E3 and E12-E13 are only PROPOSED text and identical in kind across the five).

1. pmi-geomargin-l1-rq - the only proposal whose behaviour table is popularity-adjusted on both out-degree and successor in-degree (1/sqrt(out_i*in_j+eps)) and refreshed online by a per-step scatter-add, which is what E5's skew (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543, Spearman -0.973) calls for; its weight w = rho_off*mean_scale/max_k log(1+b_k) caps the offset at exactly 10% of the measured mean min_k D_k, i.e. scaled to the local geodesic margin, so it perturbs a measured fraction of cells instead of collapsing them as l1_br did (E6 recall 0.04671); BEHAVIOUR_OFF sets the surplus constant and forces off_k=0 exactly, GEOMETRY_OFF gives d=2||u-q||, so the three switches are real.
2. l1pdo-rq - the only one combining a live geometry->behaviour->geometry loop (demand is an EMA of in-degree carried by the same curved softmax) with c=1, typical ball norm tanh(1)=0.762, so the curvature is not the near-Euclidean no-op that E6's mild geodesic arms show (successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500 against baseline 0.0555); its offset is zero-mean and symmetric (beta*clip(.,+-ln3), beta = the baseline commitment default) so it cannot one-sidedly drag mass onto hubs; cost and switch logic are fully specified.
3. BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ - correct metric bookkeeping (offset added to a length, s_D = mean_i min_k D_ik, so the behaviour/geometry balance is curvature-invariant, the right reading of E12 that R_c = 1/sqrt c sets the distance unit) and demand measured through the curved soft assignment; but its own c=0.25 gives sqrt(c)||x||~0.23-0.5 and lambda = 1/72000 is one e-fold over the whole 72000 steps, so demand stays near its init and the geometry is the mild regime E6 shows produced no recall movement.
4. GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ - cleanest switch fidelity (zero-mean z makes behaviour-off literally the baseline argmin) and a distance-derived weight (max offset = theta*Dbar = 10% of the typical coding distance), but z is frozen from a pre-pass that uses the BASELINE Euclidean level-1 assignments (E1-E2), so curvature never enters the behaviour statistic - the coupling is weaker than the pmi/l1pdo loop - and c=1 with a 10% cap on a stiff artanh metric is the most likely of the five to change no argmin, matching E6's 0.05500/0.05463 geodesic-successor arms.
5. DEMARGIN-L1-CURV - ranked last because its offset scale w = mean_i[(max_k D_ik - min_k D_ik)/2] is the full nearest-to-farthest distance half-spread, far larger than the local nearest-code margin, and the offset is clamped to [0, 3w] and hence one-sided: it is the largest and least controlled displacement of the five, the regime E6 shows is destructive (l1_br 0.04671 vs baseline 0.0555, and E8 caps the K=256 first-level share at 0.0822); it also admits frozen s drift toward the ball boundary where atanh explodes.

OBJECTION (recorded with the ranking): every proposal leaves K1=256 and every level-2/3 step at baseline, yet the frozen evidence locates the loss beyond level 1 - E6/E7 show l1_br has gold prefix alive 1.000/1.000/1.000 at depths 1-3 with the target SID in the beams only 0.0678 (attrition at depth 4), and l1_br_euclid, the strongest frozen arm, loses at depths 2/3 (0.829/0.161); the best o

bserved recalls (l1_only 0.06233, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, resample 0.06363) come from arms with no behaviour term and no curvature, while behaviour-geodesic level-1 arms sit at 0.0546-0.0550; E8 additionally caps the K=256 first-level pair-sharing rate at 0.0822. So a level-1-only curved behaviour margin has bounded headroom below the 0.065 target, and the top-ranked candidate's 10%-of-typical-distance cap may be too small to flip enough assignments to beat single-seed noise, with no ablation, sweep or seed repetition permitted to establish which term acted.
END OF ANSWER.
